title: Deploy & Domain
summary: Deploy means a public link — keep secrets in Environment Variables, not in code.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **What will you understand?** **How to deploy your app with a public link** — **and keep secrets in a safe place**.
- **Why now?** **You have built an interface, a database, and AI** — **but it’s still on localhost**. **Only you can use it**.
- **What after the lesson?** **You will distinguish between what is 'public' (link, name)** **and what is 'secret' (API keys)**.

sections.heading: Tension — A good app — but trapped on your device
sections.subtitle: A good app — but trapped on your device
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Everything works on `localhost`** — **but no one in the world can access it**.
- **You send `localhost:5173` to your friend** — **it won’t open for them**. **The app is still just an idea on your device**.
- **Deploy** = **make it available on the internet**. **But the OpenAI key must remain secret** — **not in the code**.

sections.heading: Core idea — Public link + Protected secrets
sections.subtitle: Public link + Protected secrets
sections.contentMarkdown:
- **Deploy** = **the code goes to a server** — **people access it from a public URL** (like `my-app.com`).
- **Secrets (API keys, database keys)** **go to a 'vault' on the server** — **Environment Variables** — **not in GitHub**.
- **The difference:** **what people see (link, interface)** **versus what must remain hidden (keys)**.

sections.heading: Comparison — Key in code vs Key in vault
sections.subtitle: Key in code vs Key in vault
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Secret in code | Secret in Env Vars |
|----------------|------------------|
| **OpenAI key in a file on GitHub** — **anyone can see it and use it on your account**. **Financial and security disaster** | **Code is public — keys are only in the server vault**. **The link is public, secrets are protected** |

sections.heading: Glossary — Two terms to start
sections.subtitle: Two terms to start
sections.contentMarkdown:
| Term | Meaning | Example |
|------|---------|---------|
| **Deploy** | **Move the app from your device to a server** — **a public URL that anyone can access** | **From localhost → `https://my-ai-app.com`** |
| **Environment Variables** | **A vault for secrets on the server** — **API keys and database passwords** | **OPENAI_API_KEY in Production settings** — **not in the code** |

sections.heading: Screenshot block (intent)
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Build log — successful deployment:**

Every deploy = **a new version on the internet**. **The build log shows what succeeded and what failed** — **not a black box**.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Check
sections.subtitle: Quick Check
sections.contentMarkdown:
> **Quiz key (unchanged):** correctIndex: 0

**Question:** **The app runs on your device. What is the most critical thing you might forget before deployment?**

**API keys in the Production vault** — **not in the code or GitHub**.
The color of the 'Submit' button in the interface**.**
The number of 404 pages**.**

**Explanation:** **Wrong secrets = the app crashes or gets stolen**. **The link is public — and secrets must stay in the vault**.

sections.heading: Mission — List: Public vs Secret
sections.subtitle: List: Public vs Secret
sections.contentMarkdown:
**Introduction:** **Before Deploy — distinguish what people see from what must remain hidden**. **10 minutes**.

**Submission:** **3 public items**, **3 secrets**, **which secret would be the most dangerous if leaked** and why.

**Evaluation Criteria:**

| Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| Correct Classification | 60% | **3 public (URL, interface, public content)**; **3 secrets (API keys, DB password, JWT secret)** |
| Risk Priority | 40% | **Most dangerous secret due to logic (money, user data, ...)** |
